definition: Full-screen Windows crash that halts the OS after an unrecoverable fault, most often a bad driver or poorly seated RAM, and may write a memory dump.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

definition: Repeated, unplanned power-offs of a Windows PC, traced through kernel and EventLog entries in Event Viewer to failing hardware, a faulty driver, power settings, or bad power.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Background Windows components that fail at boot, logged as Event ID 7000 by the Service Control Manager, often because of a wrong logon account or a resource conflict.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Windows programs that close unexpectedly, investigated in Reliability Monitor and the Application log, then fixed with a vendor patch, a repair, or a reinstall.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: A Windows PC that freezes, errors, or reboots at random, whose overall stability score and history of failures can be traced day by day in Reliability Monitor.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Startup error where the firmware finds no bootable drive, often because a USB stick is first in the boot order or the boot files are damaged.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

definition: A Windows PC that has gradually become slow, diagnosed by checking CPU, memory, disk, network, and GPU use in Task Manager and Resource Monitor.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Windows message that RAM and the paging file are nearly used up, caused by too little installed memory or one process using far more than normal.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Windows error that too many devices on one controller have used up its endpoints or power budget; fix it by moving slow devices to other ports.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Long logon caused by a bloated roaming profile crossing the network, login scripts, Group Policy, startup items, or a clock out of sync with the domain.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Gradual gap between a computer's real-time clock and the true time, which can break domain logons and certificates; fix it by syncing with an NTP server.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Hidden file on a drive where Windows moves idle memory pages when physical RAM fills, usually set to about 1.5 times the installed RAM.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Fix for a corrupt or slow user environment: back up the user's data, delete the profile in System Properties, and let Windows create a new one at the next logon.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Removing a recently installed Windows patch from Update history when it causes problems, or reverting to a restore point taken before it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Device Manager button on a device's Driver tab that returns to the previously installed version after a new one causes errors such as a blue screen.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

definition: Windows recovery option that reinstalls the operating system from a local copy or a cloud download, either keeping personal files or removing everything.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Windows Recovery Environment tool that automatically fixes problems that stop Windows from booting, much like running bootrec /rebuildbcd.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against Docter – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: First Windows startup program run by the UEFI firmware; it reads the stored boot settings and starts the OS loader, or offers a choice of systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against Docter – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Store that lists the installed operating systems and where their files are, read by bootmgr at startup and edited with bcdedit or rebuilt with bootrec.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Default crash file Windows writes after a fatal error, holding only the RAM the kernel was using, saved as Memory.dmp in the system root.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

definition: Smallest crash file option, holding only basic error and driver details, written to its own folder under the system root for later debugging.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

definition: Crash file holding the entire contents of RAM, which needs a paging file at least as large as physical memory plus 1 MB.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 53: Troubleshooting Microsoft Windows

definition: Mobile app that will not open, often because a copy is stuck in the background or its cache is corrupt; force stop it, clear the cache, or reinstall.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Mobile app that hangs or quits on its own at random times rather than every time, fixed by force stopping it, clearing its cache and data, or reinstalling it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Mobile app stuck on an old version, often because the store updates only on Wi-Fi, automatic updates are off, or the device no longer meets its requirements.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Mobile app download that will not finish setting up, most often from too little free storage, an incompatible device or OS version, or a weak connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Mobile device or app that lags, usually from RAM filled by background apps, nearly full storage, a poor network connection, or outdated software.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Mobile system upgrade that will not complete because the hardware is no longer supported, storage cannot hold both versions, or the device is on a metered connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Phone that needs charging far too often, caused by an aging battery, apps running in the background, heat, constant signal searching, or radios left on.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Mobile device that restarts on its own; check battery health, storage over 90 percent, OS and app updates, overheating, and an Android auto restart setting.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Display stuck in portrait or landscape as the device is turned, usually because the rotation lock is on, an app locked the orientation, or a motion sensor failed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Android App info action that ends a misbehaving app and all its background processes, stronger than just swiping it away from the recent apps view.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against Exam Cram 2e – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Deleting only an app's temporary stored files, which often fixes an app that will not load after an update without removing the user's sign-in or settings.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Erasing all of an app's saved settings, sign-ins, and files so it starts as if newly installed, a stronger step than deleting only its temporary files.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Turning a mobile device off and back on, which clears running apps from memory but keeps all data; the first step for a frozen screen or app.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against Exam Cram 2e – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Returning a mobile device to its original software state, which erases all user data, apps, and settings; a last resort that needs a backup first.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against Exam Cram 2e – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: iOS Control Center setting that keeps the display upright; while it is on, the screen will not turn to landscape when the device is rotated.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Setting that slows the device and limits background activity, brightness, and radios to stretch the remaining charge.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 54: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems and Applications

definition: Alternative download source outside Google Play or the Apple App Store, whose apps skip the official review and may carry malware or never get updates.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Installing a mobile app directly from a package file instead of an official store, which bypasses its security vetting; developers do this with ADB or Xcode.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Hidden Android menu, unlocked by tapping the build number seven times, that exposes USB debugging, running services, and mock locations, weakening security if left on.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Gaining superuser control of an Android device to bypass vendor limits, which ends vendor patches and lets malware hide; MDM can block such devices.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Bypassing Apple's restrictions on an iPhone or iPad to gain full OS control and install unapproved apps, which removes built-in protections.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

definition: Mobile app with harmful intent, often given away by permissions that do not fit its purpose, such as a camera app that wants to record calls.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Harmful app that copies the name and icon of a well-known one; check the publisher, install count, and reviews before downloading.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Cracked copy of a paid app with its copy protection removed, usually shared as a package file and often bundled with malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: File format used to distribute and install Android apps; installing one from an untrusted website skips Google Play's security checks.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

definition: Long, unexplained spikes in data sent or received by a mobile device, which may mean an app is stealing data or relaying traffic through it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Security symptom in which a phone grows slow because hidden malware is consuming its processor and memory; check usage and run an antimalware scan.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Carrier alert that the plan's allowance has been exceeded unexpectedly, possibly because a hidden app is sending spam or data in the background.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Intermittent or partial online access on a mobile device that, once signal and radio firmware are ruled out, may come from malware hogging or proxying the connection.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Complete loss of online access on a phone that, after the usual causes are ruled out, may mean a malicious DNS or relay server it was pointed at went offline.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Flood of advertisements appearing outside normal apps and sites, a sign of adware from a malicious app; uninstall recent apps until they stop.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Bogus alert on a phone claiming it is infected to push the user into installing something; treat it as malware already present and factory reset the device.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: A newly installed, untrusted app acting in ways it should not; read its reviews, compare them with its install count, and scan the device for malware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Private photos, contacts, or documents from a phone turning up where they should not, a serious sign that calls for isolating the device at once.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 55: Troubleshooting Mobile Operating Systems Security Issues

definition: PC that cannot reach network resources even though its adapter works, possibly because malware changed its DNS or proxy settings or crashed while relaying traffic.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Fake dialog box made to look like a Windows system message that reports an error and urges the user to call a bogus support number or download software.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Warning that claims protection is off or a virus was found when that is untrue, shown by malware to scare the user into acting.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

definition: Malware that poses as a security scanner, reports invented infections, and demands payment or an install to clean them.
source: CompTIA A+ Certification All-in-One Exam Guide, 11th ed. – Glossary; checked against Docter – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Key OS or user files changed or replaced by malware with high privileges, so normal tasks such as printing or saving stop working.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Documents that vanish from view or get new names or extensions, a typical sign of ransomware that encrypts data and leaves a ransom note.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Errors that block users from opening or copying their own documents because malware changed the permissions or encrypted the data.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Messages in the system notification area pushed by a website the user allowed to send alerts, made to look as if they come from the OS.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Windows patches that will not install, from low disk space, bad settings, drivers, or malware; look up the error code with the update troubleshooter.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Unrequested browser window or tab that opens in front of the page, often with ads; frequent ones despite the blocker point to adware.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Browser message that a site's security credential is expired, untrusted, or issued for a different hostname, so the connection may not be safe.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Being sent to a different website than the one requested, caused by malware, a bad extension, changed DNS settings, or a hijacked home page.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues

definition: Sending users who type a correct web address to a fake look-alike site by altering the local hosts file or poisoning DNS records.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Slow page loads, crashes, and frozen tabs, caused by too many tabs or an old version, or by cryptominers, malicious scripts, extensions, or proxies.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 7: Troubleshooting Operating Systems and Security

definition: Add-on disguised as a useful tool that hijacks searches, injects ads, or steals data; remove it and install add-ons only from trusted stores.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 56: Troubleshooting PC Security Issues
